question: What is the primary purpose of diagnostic techniques in primary health care?

options.A: To identify health problems and guide treatment
options.B: To increase the cost of patient hospital stays
options.C: To eliminate all potential risks of medication
options.D: To replace the need for physical examinations

explanation: Diagnostics are tools used to figure out what is wrong with a patient so the correct treatment can be started. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T4#GNS124_U6_T4_h1)

question: Why do diagnostic tools in primary health care need to be simple and affordable?

options.A: Laboratory tests are always completely inaccurate
options.B: Primary care centers have limited resources and high community needs
options.C: Nurses are not allowed to use expensive equipment
options.D: Patients in rural communities rarely get sick

explanation: Primary health care serves everyday people with tight budgets, so we need accessible and cost-effective tools that work well in our local clinics. Great job thinking practically! [learn more](GNS124_U6_T4#GNS124_U6_T4_h1)

question: What physical examination technique involves using a stethoscope to listen to internal body sounds?
explanation: Auscultation is the act of listening to sounds within the body, such as the heart and lungs, using a stethoscope. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T4#GNS124_U6_T4_h2)

question: A nurse is gently pressing on a patient's abdomen to check for tenderness and masses. Which physical examination technique is the nurse using?
explanation: Palpation involves using the hands and fingers to feel parts of the body for tenderness, lumps, or abnormal size. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T4#GNS124_U6_T4_h2)

question: Which common blood test checks for both anemia and signs of infection?
explanation: A Complete Blood Count (CBC) looks at your red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets. It is super helpful for spotting anemia and infections! Keep it up. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T4#GNS124_U6_T4_h3)

question: Why must a laboratory result always be compared with the patient's physical condition?

options.B: Patients usually lie about their symptoms
options.C: Lab values alone do not tell the whole clinical story
options.D: Doctors refuse to read raw lab reports

explanation: A number on a lab sheet is only one piece of the puzzle and must match how the patient actually feels and looks. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T4#GNS124_U6_T4_h3)

question: What is a major advantage of Rapid Diagnostic Tests in primary health care?

options.A: They provide quick results with minimal equipment
options.B: They eliminate the need for clinical history taking
options.C: They are completely free to manufacture worldwide

explanation: RDTs are designed to give fast answers at the bedside or in remote clinics without needing heavy laboratory machinery. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T4#GNS124_U6_T4_h4)

question: What should a nurse typically do after a patient gets a positive result on a screening RDT?

options.B: Throw away all the remaining test kits
options.C: Ignore the result and send the patient home
options.D: Perform a confirmatory test if required by guidelines

explanation: Screening tests can sometimes give false positives, so important diagnoses often require a second confirmatory test. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T4#GNS124_U6_T4_h4)

question: When is the best time to label a collected laboratory specimen?

options.B: After returning to the nursing station at the end of the shift
options.C: Immediately at the bedside after collection
options.D: After the laboratory results are printed

explanation: Labeling samples right at the bedside prevents dangerous mix-ups between different patients' tubes. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T4#GNS124_U6_T4_h5)

question: Why is prompt transportation of a biological specimen to the laboratory important?

options.A: To reduce the cost of electricity in the clinic
options.B: To ensure the requisition form does not get lost
options.C: To prevent sample degradation or bacterial overgrowth
options.D: To make sure the laboratory staff stay busy

explanation: Leaving samples sitting out too long ruins cells and allows bacteria to multiply, leading to false test results. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T4#GNS124_U6_T4_h5)

question: Where should a nurse immediately dispose of a used injection needle after drawing blood?

options.A: In an open plastic trash bin

explanation: Sharps boxes are specially designed to prevent accidental needle stick injuries to healthcare workers and cleaners. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T4#GNS124_U6_T4_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a safe infection control practice during specimen collection?

options.A: Recapping used needles with both hands before disposal
options.B: Treating all biological specimens as potentially infectious
options.C: Performing hand hygiene before and after the procedure
options.D: Wearing clean gloves when handling blood samples

explanation: Recapping used needles is a major cause of accidental needle stick injuries and should be avoided; needles go straight into the safety box uncapped. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T4#GNS124_U6_T4_h6)
